The relevant fix is likely in commit related to "Fix use-after-free in xmlParserPrintFileContextInternal" or similar. Let me think about the root cause.

The vulnerability: when parsing entities, the parser input buffer can be freed, but `ctxt->input` still points to it. When an error is reported via `xmlReportError`/`__xmlRaiseError`, it calls `xmlParserPrintFileContextInternal(input, ...)` which reads `input->cur`, `input->base`, `input->end` - pointers into freed memory.

Let me look at how the fix was done. Let me check the actual libxml2 fix for this oss-fuzz issue. The issue id is 42529030. Let me search online.

  * ####  [ parser: Pass userData to SAX text callbacks in xmlParseReference ](/GNOME/libxml2/commit/226b560837b90dea9b14431eca6e6fda8fb01ab4 "parser: Pass userData to SAX text callbacks in xmlParseReference

When replaceEntities is on and the entity's cached tree is reused,
the first/last text-child optimization in xmlParseReference called
ctxt->sax->characters / cdataBlock with ctxt as the first argument
instead of ctxt->userData. Every other SAX callsite in parser.c
correctly passes ctxt->userData.

With xmlSchemaSAXPlug installed \(as set up by
xmlTextReaderSetSchema / xmlTextReaderSchemaValidate\), userData is
a _xmlSchemaSAXPlug*, so handing over a raw ctxt to the registered
charactersSplit handler produces a type-confused dereference:
charactersSplit reads ctxt->myDoc as user_sax and ctxt->myDoc->URL
as user_sax->characters, then calls that string pointer as code.
The result is a reliable SIGSEGV on the first entity reference in
any XSD-validated xmlTextReader stream \(and a silent validation
bypass on the rare targets where the confused call doesn't crash\).

Fix by passing ctxt->userData, matching the rest of the file.")

###  Commits on Jun 22, 2025 

  * ####  [ parser: Don't load external content if only XML_SKIP_IDS is set ](/GNOME/libxml2/commit/e7802738c619a15f55174bac3246ae82602f2d46 "parser: Don't load external content if only XML_SKIP_IDS is set

At some point, the `loadsubset` member was augmented to also control
handling of ID attributes in addition to loading of external DTDs. These
two features are unrelated and shouldn't have been mixed. This mistake
was probably inspired by the misnamed XML_DETECT_IDS flag. As a side
effect, setting XML_SKIP_IDS always enabled loading of external DTDs and
parameter entities.

This change makes it possible to ignore IDs without loading external
content. This is a deliberate API change that improves security and is
unlikely to affect users.

This also makes sure that the new XML_PARSE_SKIP_IDS option doesn't
enable unsafe behavior.")

parser: Pass userData to SAX text callbacks in xmlParseReference

When replaceEntities is on and the entity's cached tree is reused,
the first/last text-child optimization in xmlParseReference called
ctxt->sax->characters / cdataBlock with ctxt as the first argument
instead of ctxt->userData. Every other SAX callsite in parser.c
correctly passes ctxt->userData.

With xmlSchemaSAXPlug installed (as set up by
xmlTextReaderSetSchema / xmlTextReaderSchemaValidate), userData is
a _xmlSchemaSAXPlug*, so handing over a raw ctxt to the registered
charactersSplit handler produces a type-confused dereference:
charactersSplit reads ctxt->myDoc as user_sax and ctxt->myDoc->URL
as user_sax->characters, then calls that string pointer as code.
The result is a reliable SIGSEGV on the first entity reference in
any XSD-validated xmlTextReader stream (and a silent validation
bypass on the rare targets where the confused call doesn't crash).

Fix by passing ctxt->userData, matching the rest of the file.

parser: Fix infinite loop in xmlCtxtParseContent

The loop to find an element/document ancestor uses "cur = node->parent"
as the iterator instead of "cur = cur->parent". This causes an infinite
loop when the immediate parent is not an element/document/html node
(e.g., when the node's parent is an entity reference).

Fix by iterating with cur->parent to properly walk up the ancestor chain.

parser: Don't load external content if only XML_SKIP_IDS is set

At some point, the `loadsubset` member was augmented to also control
handling of ID attributes in addition to loading of external DTDs. These
two features are unrelated and shouldn't have been mixed. This mistake
was probably inspired by the misnamed XML_DETECT_IDS flag. As a side
effect, setting XML_SKIP_IDS always enabled loading of external DTDs and
parameter entities.

This change makes it possible to ignore IDs without loading external
content. This is a deliberate API change that improves security and is
unlikely to affect users.

This also makes sure that the new XML_PARSE_SKIP_IDS option doesn't
enable unsafe behavior.

name.value: parser: Pass userData to SAX text callbacks in xmlParseReference

value.value: parser: Pass userData to SAX text callbacks in xmlParseReference

parser: Pass userData to SAX text callbacks in xmlParseReference

When replaceEntities is on and the entity's cached tree is reused,
the first/last text-child optimization in xmlParseReference called
ctxt->sax->characters / cdataBlock with ctxt as the first argument
instead of ctxt->userData. Every other SAX callsite in parser.c
correctly passes ctxt->userData.

With xmlSchemaSAXPlug installed (as set up by
xmlTextReaderSetSchema / xmlTextReaderSchemaValidate), userData is
a _xmlSchemaSAXPlug*, so handing over a raw ctxt to the registered
charactersSplit handler produces a type-confused dereference:
charactersSplit reads ctxt->myDoc as user_sax and ctxt->myDoc->URL
as user_sax->characters, then calls that string pointer as code.
The result is a reliable SIGSEGV on the first entity reference in
any XSD-validated xmlTextReader stream (and a silent validation
bypass on the rare targets where the confused call doesn't crash).

Fix by passing ctxt->userData, matching the rest of the file.

parser: Fix infinite loop in xmlCtxtParseContent

The loop to find an element/document ancestor uses "cur = node->parent"
as the iterator instead of "cur = cur->parent". This causes an infinite
loop when the immediate parent is not an element/document/html node
(e.g., when the node's parent is an entity reference).

Fix by iterating with cur->parent to properly walk up the ancestor chain.

Add regression test to testparser.c.

Fixes: 4f329dc5 ("parser: Implement xmlCtxtParseContent")

name.value: parser: Don't load external content if only XML_SKIP_IDS is set

value.value: parser: Don't load external content if only XML_SKIP_IDS is set

parser: Don't load external content if only XML_SKIP_IDS is set

At some point, the `loadsubset` member was augmented to also control
handling of ID attributes in addition to loading of external DTDs. These
two features are unrelated and shouldn't have been mixed. This mistake
was probably inspired by the misnamed XML_DETECT_IDS flag. As a side
effect, setting XML_SKIP_IDS always enabled loading of external DTDs and
parameter entities.

This change makes it possible to ignore IDs without loading external
content. This is a deliberate API change that improves security and is
unlikely to affect users.

This also makes sure that the new XML_PARSE_SKIP_IDS option doesn't
enable unsafe behavior.

content:
Correctly relocate internal pointers after realloc()

Adding an offset to a deallocated pointer and assuming that it can be
dereferenced is undefined behaviour. When running libxml2 on CHERI-enabled
systems such as Arm Morello this results in the creation of an out-of-bounds
pointer that cannot be dereferenced and therefore crashes at runtime.

The effect of this UB is not just limited to architectures such as CHERI,
incorrect relocation of pointers after realloc can in fact cause
FORTIFY_SOURCE errors with recent GCC:
https://developers.redhat.com/articles/2022/09/17/gccs-new-fortification-level
===FILES===
parser.c modified
@@ -9582,10 +9582,10 @@ xmlParseStartTag2(xmlParserCtxtPtr ctxt, const xmlChar **pref,
              * Arithmetic on dangling pointers is technically undefined
              * behavior, but well...
              */
-            ptrdiff_t offset = ctxt->input->base - atts[i+2];
+            const xmlChar *old = atts[i+2];
             atts[i+2]  = NULL;    /* Reset repurposed namespace URI */
-            atts[i+3] += offset;  /* value */
-            atts[i+4] += offset;  /* valuend */
+            atts[i+3] = ctxt->input->base + (atts[i+3] - old);  /* value */
+            atts[i+4] = ctxt->input->base + (atts[i+4] - old);  /* valuend */
         }
